At 40o latitude, this current is aﬀ ected by Westwind. It turns to east and current coming from the south i.e, Falklands Current meets with the Brazil current. This current moving ahead and meeting with South Equatorial current forms a complete circle of currents. This complete circle of currents ﬂ ow in anticlock- wise direction. What explains the eastward ﬂ ow of the equatorial counter-current? (a) The Earth's rotation on its axis (b) Convergence of the two equatorial currents (c) Diﬀ erence in salinity of water (d) Occurrence of the Belt of Calm near the equator I.A.S. (Pre) 2015 Ans. (a) There are two equatorial currents ﬂ owing from east to west – the north equatorial current and the south equatorial current. In between these two, there ﬂ ows an equatorial counter current in the opposite direction from west to east. Piling up of water due to the convergence of two equatorial currents give rise to equatorial counter current. Therefore, its the earth rotation on its axis which is responsible for the eastward ﬂ ow of equatorial counter current. Salinity of the Ocean Almost every known chemical element can be found in varying proportion in the ocean. *Salinity is the amount of salt dissolved in a body of water. On average, seawater in the world’s oceans has a salinity of approximately 35‰ or 35 parts per thousand. This means that for every 1 litre (1000 ml) of seawater there are 35 gms of salt dissolved in it. *Lands are the main source of salinity of the oceans and rivers are the main carriers. Other factors responsible for ocean salinity are - evaporation, wind, River water, Precipitation, ocean currents, volcanoes etc. *During an exploration of Challenger Deep in 1884, Dittmar, ﬁ gured out that there are 27 types of salts present in the seas. Out of these 27 salts, 7 are the important ones. They are as follows. Salt Salinity (‰) Percentage (%) Sodium Chloride 27.213 77.8 Magnesium Chloride 3.80 10.9 Magnesium Sulphate 1.658 4.7 Calcium Sulphate 1.260 3.6 Potassium Sulphate 0.863 2.5 Calcium Carbonate 0.123 0.3 Magnesium Bromide 0.076 0.2 *The maximum contribution to the salinity of the ocean is that of sodium chloride. *The salinity of the ocean can be divided into horizontal and vertical parameters. The uncertainty with the amount of salinity in the vertical sphere has obstructed in ﬁ nding a principle for measuring vertical salinity. It is because at some places salinity increases with depth and vice-versa. *The density of Ocean water is directly proportional to its salinity. It means that if the density of water increases it is an indicator of an increase in salinity hence with the increase in water density, salinity also increases. *The horizontal distribution of salinity in ocean’s water is expressed as the degree of saltiness of the water, either as a percentage or more often in parts per thousand variations are shown in salinity distribution maps by isohalines (lines joining places having an equal degree of salinity). The Latitudes have a huge impact on the salinity of the oceans. Salinity is lower than the average 36‰ in equatorial waters because of the heavy daily rainfall and high relative humidity. The water fringing the High- Pressure Belts of the trade winds Deserts between 20º and 40º N and S, have high salinity because of the high rate of evaporation caused by high temperature and low humidity. Waters of the polar region have salinity of less than 35‰ because of the colder climate with little evaporation and because much fresh water is added from the melting of icebergs as well as by several large pole ward-bound rivers, e.g. ob, Lena, Yenisei etc. *Maximum salinity is found between 20º-40º North Latitudes where salinity may increase up to 36‰. *Ocean water of the Indian Ocean falling between 0º-10º Latitudes have a salinity of 35.14‰ however it decreases to 30‰ in Bay of Bengal. On the contrary the salinity increases upto 36‰ in the Arabian Sea. It is because of high rate of evaporation and low humidity. Also there is much less fresh water carried to the Arabian sea by west ﬂ owing rivers as compared to Bay of Bengal. *Among the various seas and Lakes of the world, the Van Lake of Turkey has a salinity of 330‰. The salinity of Dead sea is 238‰. *Salinity in the Northern part of Caspian sea is 14‰ whereas in the southern part of Caspian sea, in the Karabuga Bay, salinity is 17‰. *The most saline sea is Red sea with a salinity of 36-41‰. *The salinity of the Mediterranean Sea is 37-39‰. In the Caribbean Sea it is 35-36‰ and the salinity of the Persian Gulf is 37-40‰. High Tide, Low Tide *Tides are the rise and fall of sea levels caused by the combined eﬀ ects of the gravitational forces exerted by the Moon and the Sun, and the rotation of the Earth. The rotation of the Earth creates two forces - the Centripetal and Centrifugal force, which plays a major role in the formation of Tides. It means that the side of the earth which faces the moon experiences a gravitational force, greater than that of the earth itself. Hence we experience spring Tides. On the other hand the side of earth which is facing away from moon experiences less gravitational force from the moon, as a result, we experience Neap Tides. Thus in the time span of 24 hrs. we experience two Spring Tides and two Neap Tides. Moon Syzygy Sun Moon Moon Sun Moon *When the Sun, the Moon and the Earth are aligned in a straight line, then we experience a High Tide. In astronomy, the situation is known as syzygy. It happens on a full moon Join−> https://t.me/thehindu000 CB–122 General Studies World Geography or new moon day. On the other hand, when the sun, the moon and the earth are at a right angle to each other then the gravitational forces of these celestial bodies act against each other as a result of which we experience low tides. Low tide is seen on the 7th or 8th day of each lunar month (14 days apx.) During Low Tides, there is a decrease of 20% in the spring Tides whereas the Neap Tides are higher than the normal occurrences. *The moon is the closest celestial body to earth hence its gravity has a huge impact on our planet. The moon is responsible for the sea waves of the oceans. *The eﬀ ect of Moon on the tidal forces of our planet is 2.17 times more than that of the sun. *The city of South Hampton of England experiences 4 tides every day. (a) Due to the eﬀ ect of the sun (b) Due to the rotation of the Earth (c) Due to the combined eﬀ ect of sun and the moon (d) Due to Gravitation, Centripetal force and the centrifugal force U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1991 Ans. (d) High tide/low tide occurs as a result of the force of gravitational pull between the Earth and the Moon and the two forces viz centripetal force and centrifugal force produced upon the Earth. Ocean water is kept at equal levels around the planet by the Earth's gravity pulling inward, but Moon's gravitational force is strong enough to disrupt this balance by accelerating the water in that hemisphere which faces the Moon. When the Moon's force of attraction is stronger than the centrifugal force of the Earth, high tides occur. On the other hand, when the centrifugal force is stronger than the Moon's force of attraction tides (Indirect high tide) occur. Earth experiences high and low tides twice in 24 hours. 2. Tide producing power of the moon is 2.17 times more than the Sun. The Oceanic Trenches Oceanic Trenches are long narrow trenches that plunge as great deeps to a depth of 5000 fathoms or 30000 feet. Trenches accounts for approximately 7% of the ocean’s relief contrary to our expectations most of the deepest trenches are not located in the midst of the ocean. They are more often found close to the continents, particularly in the Paciﬁ c Ocean, where several deep trenches have been founded. *Mariana Trench is the deepest trench in the world. It is located in the Paciﬁ c Ocean east of Mariana Islands. The Mariana Trench or Challenger deep is a crescent- shaped trough. This trench was discovered in 1948 with the help of a survey ship called HMS challenger 2. The speculated Depth of the Mariana Trench is 11,033 mts.
